comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological approach (C17, C20-C22, C73, C95-C97). Both evaluations find the cell type mapping methodology using AHBA data, Gaussian process regression, and BRETIGEA deconvolution to be sound and well-supported. OpenEval provides technical details while peer reviewers describe it as 'innovative methods' providing 'convincing evidence.'

Strong agreement on core statistical findings (C23, C29, C39, C44, C48-C49, C60, C83). Both evaluations support the correlations between cell type distributions and atrophy patterns with appropriate FDR correction. OpenEval emphasizes the ALS-specific positive neuronal correlation (C49), while peer reviewers focus on AD/FTD associations with astrocytes and microglia. Both accept the hierarchical clustering results.

Agreement on clustering patterns (C53-C54, C56-C58, C67). Both evaluations support the hierarchical clustering findings including EOAD/PS1 grouping and FTD clinical variant stratification. OpenEval notes C59 (hierarchical clustering analysis) while peer review references it indirectly. Both acknowledge the separation of conditions despite shared pathologies (C67) as meaningful.

Agreement on study limitations (C87-C93). Both evaluations accept the author-acknowledged limitations as reasonable caveats rather than fatal flaws. OpenEval explicitly lists seven specific limitations with citations, while peer reviewers implicitly accept them by endorsing the study as 'valuable' despite these constraints.

Disagreement on broad mechanistic conclusion (C77, C19). OpenEval rates C77 as UNCERTAIN, noting it extends beyond correlational data and lacks direct mechanistic validation in diseased tissue. Peer reviewers (R4) explicitly endorse this conclusion as SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 reiterating agreement about surpassing 'neuro-centric view.' This represents a key divergence in interpretation of what the data can support.

Disagreement on ALS protective interpretation (C50). OpenEval rates C50 as UNCERTAIN, calling the 'protective effect' interpretation speculative without mechanistic validation. Peer reviewers accept this interpretation as SUPPORTED without specific comment, treating it as part of the accepted findings framework.

Partial agreement on network topology inference (C71). OpenEval rates C71 as UNCERTAIN but notes it's a 'reasonable interpretation supported by cited literature.' Peer reviewers implicitly support this inference through acceptance of clustering results and disease comparison framework. Both see value but OpenEval is more cautious about mechanistic claims.

Disagreement on FTD/PD supportive cell association (C52). OpenEval rates C52 as UNCERTAIN, noting it's based on weak correlations lacking direct evidence. Peer reviewers accept this as SUPPORTED, with implicit endorsement through acceptance of FTD stratification and disease comparison framework.

Both address main study conclusion (C19) but with different emphasis. OpenEval supports C19 with caveat about correlational nature (healthy brain distributions vs disease atrophy). Peer reviewers enthusiastically endorse this as central conclusion with 'convincing evidence.' Agreement on finding but different levels of interpretive caution.

Agreement on negative findings regarding shared pathologies (C65, C67). Both evaluations support that conditions with similar protein pathologies (DLB/PD, ALS/FTLD) show different cellular vulnerability patterns. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of C65-C70, while peer review addresses subset through clustering acceptance.

Both address contextualization with prior literature (C78-C86 in OpenEval, C83 overlap). OpenEval explicitly evaluates how findings align with prior studies showing increased non-neuronal proportions in atrophied regions. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through endorsement of core findings without questioning the literature context.

Agreement on robustness analyses (C98-C99). Both evaluations support the methodological validation showing independence from smoothing and parcellation parameters. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as strengthening confidence, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through absence of methodological concerns and praise of 'innovative methods.'
